repairs.value: The appeal to order need not depend on gaps in current scientific explanation. Mathematically describable laws, stable causal regularities, and minds capable of discovering them together invite a deeper question about why reality is intelligible. A personal source gains support only comparatively, if it makes this intelligibility more expected than brute law does without adding unsupported claims about intervention or scripture. Scientific progress therefore does not necessarily dissolve the argument; it reveals more of the stable structure whose ultimate modal explanation remains genuinely contested.
repairs.rationale: This revision preserves the comparative inference from intelligibility while retaining its evidential limits and avoiding dependence on temporary scientific ignorance.
